posts.text:
Ledn co-founder Mauricio Di Bartolomeo on how options dealers hedging short calls become forced $BTC buyers

"When somebody sells a call at, say, 90, 95 percent, the dealer that sold that call is short Bitcoin. That person basically sold somebody the right to buy Bitcoin at a particular price."

"As the price gets closer to 95, that dealer has to start buying Bitcoin to hedge that position so that they can deliver the Bitcoin to the person who will exercise that right."

"The dealers who sold those calls have to start frantically buying back more Bitcoin to have enough to deliver the Bitcoin at 95 and not have to buy it at a higher price. And so they become forced buyers."

"We usually call it a cascade down, but it's a cascade up. It happens up too."

"But when the Bitcoin price rises, your LTV drops and you have the option to redeem that excess collateral."

Matt discusses the current situation but I think It’s really about going forward.  If new unsecured debt in the AI space is being priced at 15%, that’s basically saying capital isn’t going to fund these companies again.  So the companies that are bleeding cash will have to use equity to finance 2-3 more years of operating losses and severely dilute current shareholders.  Yes the projects and chips may survive but that may end up being owned by the securitized debt holders and equity may get wrecked in the process.   Now on top of that you’re seeing secured debt getting priced at 10% now too (see FT article).  Add on some delays, political pushback, permitting issues, and investor concerns about risks and you can run into a situation where private equity doesn’t get paid back anytime soon.  So it’s not “panic”, it’s repricing.  And the reprice may not be so great.   This benefits the companies that are financing a lot of their capex via legacy free cash flow.  The debt heavy new incumbents may have problems.

quoted.text:
CoreWeave's debt, explained simply, because I like to speak plainly:

Secured debt = the mortgage. Backed by the house. The GPUs and the contracts they serve are the collateral. 

Unsecured debt = the credit card. 

Backed by a promise.

Everyone is panicking that $CRWV UNSECURED yield to MATURITY hit 15%

But a credit card rate spiking doesn't mean the house (or in this case the GPUs/data centers) lost value. 

The secured lenders or the ones who underwrote the actual GPUs and contracts aren't selling here. 

Now zoom out, because this is analogous to the entire AI market in wrapped up in a single company. 

Trillions in secured, asset-backed debt are loaned against GPUs, data centers, power contracts, and signed capacity deals with hyperscalers. This money doesn't care about stock prices or investor sentiment. 

It gets paid if the contracts pay. (Sounds pretty similar to $next if you ask me…)

Below that in line is unsecured debt, a bet on the companies themselves.

On top of everything is the equity, a bet on the story.

So when you see scary headlines about "AI debt," ask one question: which layer?

Yields spiking on unsecured debt and equities dropping while secured debt sits calm simply means the market is repricing the story. 

The assets are fine. 

The buildout keeps getting funded because the secured debt holders still believes in the collateral.

The day that changes… well the day secured lenders start questioning GPU values and contract quality, is the day the AI

posts.name: Cullen Roche
posts.text:
It’s becoming clear that MMTers have a worse understanding of reserve accounting than we thought. 

What matters is the total remittances, not IORB in isolation. And yes, in recent years the Fed has been operating at a loss, which has been net stimulative relative to the large positive remittances of prior years even though this income effect was offset by the tighter credit conditions that accompanied the rate hikes, which were a clear net drag and help explain why inflation fell after 2022.

What’s even more off-base about the idea that this might cause inflation is that the remittances matter in rate of change, not just levels. Saying “there’s $500B of new income because of IORB” doesn’t mean we got inflation from it. If you got $100B every year for 5 years you don’t get ongoing inflation because the rate of change isn’t changing. And in recent years the net interest impact has been improving as the Fed’s annual losses have shrunk substantially, meaning the incremental addition to the consolidated government deficit from this channel has been getting smaller, not larger. They have the direction of the flow backwards and this exercise explains why their theory of inflation has been so wrong in recent years.

posts.text:
Saw some comments about my post on this topic 👇 🤣 

1. I am always supportive of any blockchain making any progress in any country. BTC, ETH, BNB, XRP, SOL, HYPE, ZEC, SIGN, all stablecoins, etc, you name it...

2. I was happy that SOL can advertise and get an office in Shanghai. It would open the path for others to follow. It would also indicate that "China unbanned crypto", which would be positive news for all of us. But alas, that's not quite the case yet, it seems...

3. My X post was not the trigger. It's now emerged that the Bund building ad was taken down within 10 minutes. (If you don't know, China monitors speech and media in real-time.) I only saw it on X 12-24 hours after the fact. 

4. Regardless of the outcome, it's good effort. Keep building and keep pushing adoption.

quoted.text:
Solana just had its event in China shut down.

And the funniest part is that CZ basically warned about this one day earlier.

First Solana Foundation announced that it has opened an office in Pudong, occupying one of the highest commercial office spaces

All of this in a country where crypto is heavily restricted.

A day before CZ notices Solana’s expansion and publicly comments on how surprising it is.

He says it’s amazing that Solana can advertise and open an office in China.

(Especially considering BNB Chain hasn’t been able to do the same)

Sounds pretty reasonable, right?

Well, less than 24 hours later…

The first event was supposed to take place at the Shangri-La hotel in Shanghai.

The event was scheduled to begin at 10 AM.

Instead, attendees arrived to find police officers at the venue.

You genuinely cannot make this stuff up.

Around noon, organizers sent an apology email arguing “Venue logistics considerations.”

CZ them posted:

“Sad to see. Looks like they really didn’t know the local policies?”

And reminded everyone that something similar had happened less than a year ago.

I’ve seen people joking that he snitched on them.

I actually respect Solana’s ambition to expand into one of the biggest markets

But I think there’s a difference between building blockchain infrastructure in China and publicly promoting a crypto ecosystem

This week Solana might have crossed that line and CZ is probably thinking he told them so.

posts.name: Jon Najarian
posts.text: A father's courage

quoted.text:
A 5-year-old girl plunged 49 feet from a moving cruise ship into the open ocean. Her father heard his wife screaming and raced toward the railing, only to discover that their daughter was gone.

It happened aboard the Disney Dream near the Bahamas, where a family vacation took a terrifying turn when the little girl fell from the ship’s fourth deck.

When her father realized what had happened, he jumped overboard after her, plunging nearly 50 feet into the ocean. But when he surfaced, he couldn’t see his daughter anywhere.

He began desperately calling out for her, searching the water until he finally heard her calling back. He swam toward her and managed to reach her, but they were still stranded in the open ocean as the massive cruise ship began turning around.

For roughly 20 minutes, he kept his little girl afloat, holding her above the water until a rescue boat finally reached them and brought them back to safety.

Both survived, although the father suffered two fractures in his spine from the fall.

It takes an incredible amount of courage to jump nearly 50 feet into the open ocean, not knowing what awaits you below. But this father didn’t hesitate to put his own life on the line for his little girl. Thank God they both made it home.
